(a) 
The sums reserved in section 304(a) for the purposes of this section shall be used for making special project grants or providing teacher-training grants in accordance with this section.
 
    (b) 
The Commissioner is authorized to make grants to local educational agencies or other public or private nonprofit agencies, including educational television stations, for special projects which will be carried out in furtherance of the purposes of this title, and which—

        (1) 
involve the use of innovative methods, systems, materials, or programs which the Commissioner determines may have national significance or be of special value in promoting effective programs under this title, or
 
        (2) 
involve programs of adult education, carried out in cooperation with other Federal, federally assisted, State, or local programs which the Commissioner determines have unusual promise in promoting a comprehensive or coordinated approach to the problems of persons with basic educational deficiencies.
   The Commissioner shall establish procedures for making grants under this subsection which shall require a non-Federal contribution of at least 10 per centum of the costs of such projects wherever feasible and not inconsistent with the purposes of this subsection.

    (c) 
The Commissioner is authorized to provide (directly or by contract), or to make grants to colleges or universities, State or local educational agencies, or other appropriate public or private nonprofit agencies or organizations, to provide training to persons engaged, or preparing to engage, as personnel in adult education programs designed to carry out the purposes of this title, with such stipends and allowances, if any (including traveling and subsistence expenses), for persons undergoing such training and their dependents as the Commissioner may by regulation determine.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is only a grant-making provision, and grant applications are not participation; the "cooperation with other Federal, federally assisted, State, or local programs" language describes grantee projects, not federal consultation. However, subsection (c) authorizes the Commissioner to set stipends and allowances "by regulation," and the definition treats authority to make rules as participation even when discretionary, because rulemaking brings in the public. The label rests on that regulatory authority, not on the grant language.
fable.s: with such stipends and allowances, if any (including traveling and subsistence expenses), for persons undergoing such training and their dependents as the Commissioner may by regulation determine

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Commissioner to make grants to outside entities and establishes procedures for those grants, including cost-sharing requirements. According to the definition, applications for benefits or grants are explicitly excluded from participation. The text describes the funding mechanism and eligibility criteria, not a process for outside parties to consult with or influence a federal decision-making body.
qwen_block.s: The Commissioner is authorized to make grants to local educational agencies or other public or private nonprofit agencies... The Commissioner shall establish procedures for making grants under this subsection which shall require a non-Federal contribution of at least 10 per centum of the costs of such projects wherever feasible and not inconsistent with the purposes of this subsection.

opus.w: The section lets the Commissioner set training stipends and allowances by regulation, and the DEFINITION treats rulemaking as participation even when it is optional (Example 6). The grant-making parts would not count on their own, because applying for grants is not participation, but the rulemaking authority makes the answer Yes.
opus.s: with such stipends and allowances, if any (including traveling and subsistence expenses), for persons undergoing such training and their dependents as the Commissioner may by regulation determine.
opus.b: 1. **The tempting wrong reading:** this section is about grants, and grant applications are not participation, so it looks like a "No." That reading misses the last clause of (c). There the Commissioner sets stipends and allowances "by regulation." The DEFINITION counts rulemaking as participation, and Example 6 counts it even when the agency only "may" use the regulatory power. Notice-and-comment rulemaking is how outside parties get a say.

This section authorizes the Commissioner to make grants, which is a funding mechanism, not a participatory decision-making process involving outside consultation or coordination. It looks like participation because it involves grants to outside entities.
qwen_chat.s: The Commissioner is authorized to make grants to local educational agencies or other public or private nonprofit agencies, including educational television stations, for special projects which will be carried out in furtherance of the purposes of this title
